evidence: Description of genetic instruments used

claim: The testosterone genetic variants had little correlation with sex hormone binding globulin (0.05 in men and 0.06 in women).
source: because these had little correlation with sex hormone binding globulin (0.05 in men and 0.06 in women) (Ruth et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ruth et al., 2020

claim: Sex-specific genetic associations with IHD were taken from the UK Biobank individual data after excluding those with inconsistent self-reported and genotyped sex, excess relatedness, abnormal sex chromosomes, or poor-quality genotyping.
source: Sex-specific genetic associations with IHD were taken from the UK Biobank individual data after excluding those with inconsistent self-reported and genotyped sex, excess relatedness (more than 10 putative third-degree relatives), abnormal sex chromosomes (such as XXY), or poor-quality genotyping (heterozygosity or missing rate >1.5%).
evidence: Description of data source and quality control

claim: Sex-specific associations with IHD were obtained using logistic regression adjusted for the first 20 principal components, age, and assay array.
source: The sex-specific associations with IHD obtained using logistic regression were adjusted for the first 20 principal components, age, and assay array.
evidence: Description of statistical analysis

claim: IHD was based on self-report at baseline, subsequent hospitalization diagnoses of ICD 9 410–4 or ICD10 I20-5 and death registration causes of ICD10 I20-5 up until December 2019.
source: IHD was based on self-report at baseline, subsequent hospitalization diagnoses (primary or secondary) of International Classification of Diseases (ICD) 9 410–4 or ICD10 I20-5 and death registration causes (primary or secondary) of ICD10 I20-5 up until December 2019.
evidence: Description of outcome definition

claim: The F-statistic was used to assess instrument strength, obtained using an approximation (mean of square of SNP-exposure association divided by square of its standard error).
source: The F-statistic was used to assess instrument strength, obtained using an approximation (mean of square of SNP-exposure association divided by square of its standard error) (Bowden et al., 2016a).
evidence: Description of statistical method with citation

claim: A conventional threshold for the F-statistic is 10.
source: A conventional threshold for the F-statistic is 10.
evidence: Statement of conventional statistical threshold

claim: SNPs with an F-statistic <10 were dropped.
source: SNPs with an F-statistic <10 were dropped.
evidence: Description of quality control procedure

claim: Steiger filtering was used to check the directionality between testosterone and IHD.
source: Steiger filtering was used to check the directionality between testosterone and IHD. (Hemani et al., 2017)
evidence: Description of statistical method with citation

claim: Sex-specific estimates of associations were obtained by combining SNP-specific Wald estimates using inverse variance weighting with multiplicative random effects.
source: Sex-specific estimates of the associations of genetically predicted exposures (i.e., genetically mimicked effects of statins, PCSK9 inhibitors, ezetimibe, anakinra and tocilizumab) with testosterone and IHD, as well as estimates of the associations of genetically predicted testosterone with IHD were obtained by combining SNP-specific Wald estimates (SNP on outcome divided by SNP on exposure) using inverse variance weighting (IVW) with multiplicative random effects (Burgess et al., 2013).
evidence: Description of statistical method with citation

claim: Multivariable MR was used to assess sex-specific associations of genetically predicted exposures with IHD allowing for testosterone, accounting for correlations between SNPs on the same chromosome.
source: Multivariable MR was used to assess sex-specific associations of genetically predicted exposures with IHD allowing for testosterone, accounting for correlations between SNPs on the same chromosome obtained from LDlink.
evidence: Description of statistical method

claim: The Sanderson-Windmejier multivariable conditional F-statistic was estimated to obtain a lower bound of the strength for each instrument conditional on the other exposure.
source: We estimated the Sanderson-Windmejier multivariable conditional F-statistic (Sanderson and Windmeijer, 2016) to obtain a lower bound of the strength for each instrument conditional on the other exposure,
evidence: Description of statistical method with citation

claim: The Q statistics were used to assess pleiotropy.
source: and the Q statistics to asses pleiotropy, using the WSpiller/MVMR package (Sanderson et al., 2019).
evidence: Description of statistical method with citation

claim: Multivariable MR-Egger estimates were used given the analysis is multivariable by design with few genetic variants available to mimic the effects of statins.
source: Given this analysis is multivariable by design with few genetic variants available to mimic the effects of statins, we used the multivariable MR-Egger estimates (Rees et al., 2017).
evidence: Description of methodological choice with citation

claim: MR-Egger is valid as long as the instrument strength independent of direct effect assumption holds.
source: MR-Egger is valid as long as the instrument strength independent of direct effect assumption holds (Bowden et al., 2015).
evidence: Description of method assumptions with citation

claim: Weighted median gives valid estimates when more than 50% of information comes from valid SNPs.
source: We also used a weighted median which gives valid estimates when more than 50% of information comes from valid SNPs (Bowden et al., 2016b).
evidence: Description of method assumptions with citation

claim: For exposures instrumented by correlated SNPs, weighted median or MR-Egger estimates were not given because of concerns about their interpretability.
source: However, for exposures instrumented by correlated SNPs we did not give the weighted median or MR-Egger estimates because of concerns about their interpretability (Burgess and Thompson, 2017).
evidence: Description of methodological limitation with citation

claim: A statistical significance level of 0.05 was used given this is a hypothesis driven study with a positive control.
source: Given this is a hypothesis driven study, with a positive control, we used a statistical significance level of 0.05.
evidence: Description of statistical threshold choice

claim: All statistical analysis was conducted using R version 3.6.1.
source: All statistical analysis was conducted using R version 3.6.1 (The R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria).
evidence: Description of software used

claim: The MendelianRandomization R package was used for the MR estimates.
source: The MendelianRandomization R package was used for the MR estimates.
evidence: Description of software package used

claim: Estimates of genetic associations were taken from publicly available UK Biobank summary statistics, except the associations with IHD which were based on individual level genetic associations from the UK Biobank obtained under application #42468.
source: Estimates of genetic associations were taken from publicly available UK Biobank summary statistics, except the associations with IHD which were based on individual level genetic associations from the UK Biobank obtained under application #42468.
evidence: Description of data sources

claim: All UK Biobank data were collected with fully informed consent.
source: All UK Biobank data were collected with fully informed consent.
evidence: Statement about ethical data collection
